approval.note: Advisory only. This approves no unit, no source, no law change. source427, the 425 reader experiment and the unfrozen 428 work_reader.rs were read as reference and are neither reviewed nor approved here.

answer.oneLine: The raw operation result is a premise, not a conclusion; the guarded boundary belongs to the owner's whole bracket, never to the raw read.
answer.shape: Prepay the complete bracket (read + required postchecks), carry an ordinary I/O or parse failure as provisional DATA so the mandatory rechecks run and are accounted, and fail the original scope only after those checks conclude. A budget/limit failure is terminal at the instant it occurs and forbids the rechecks.

whyNaiveSubstitutionIsWrong.mechanism: Both 428 wrappers return every failure, including WorkFailure::Operation(ReadFailure::Io(_)), as an Err out of a guarded boundary; the guard's Drop then sets ledger.failed = true.
whyNaiveSubstitutionIsWrong.consequenceInReadOne: Latching at the read (line 153) leaves the mandatory rechecks at lines 155-157 either skipped or running while every charge/spend returns Closed, i.e. unaccounted.
whyNaiveSubstitutionIsWrong.noEscape: Reserved allowance cannot be spent after closure and a replacement ledger is forbidden.

citations.quote: A fenced observation session retains originals and rechecks all relevant contributing owners even after later read/parse failures; any observed failure latches unavailability. ... All name enumeration, captures, graph edges/bytes and original-owner checks use the same authoritative operation budget; no branch-local reset. Budget/limit failure is incomplete/unavailable, never 'no ancestor' or permission to repair.
citations.settles: the read/parse versus budget asymmetry, the shared budget, and the no-reset rule

citations.quote: The raw EEXIST/AlreadyExists error alone is insufficient: a failed original-stage postcheck makes the outcome Indeterminate even when the primary syscall error is preserved.
citations.settles: that the conclusion is the conjunction of raw result and postcheck result, with the primary error preserved but not decisive

citations.quote: Any Indeterminate publication result, including AlreadyExists with failed postcheck | Latch unavailable, no winner shortcut, retry, deletion, registration or success receipt.
citations.settles: the effect-path disposition and the no-retry rule

lawAssessment.derivedConsequenceWorthStating: On the effect path, pre-reserving the postchecks is what makes the section 4 loser route reachable at all: that route needs a complete typed AlreadyExists AND Unchanged result, so if budget exhaustion can prevent the postcheck from running, every contended publication degrades to Indeterminate and unavailable. Under-reservation is self-defeating, not merely unsafe.

optionalClarification.exactEdit: add that an owner which must recheck after a fallible operation reserves those checks before beginning it
optionalClarification.reason: states the bracket rule rather than leaving it derived from section 8 plus section 4; sections 4 and 6 need no edit

dispositions.failure: budget or limit refusal (charge or spend)
dispositions.mandatoryPostchecks: NOT run - running them would be work after terminal failure
dispositions.outcome: incomplete/unavailable; never absence, 'no ancestor' or permission to repair

dispositions.mandatoryPostchecks: MUST run, from the prepaid allowance
dispositions.outcome: held as provisional data; reported only if every postcheck passes

errorPrecedence.oneLine: Budget failure is terminal in time; postcheck failure outranks the held raw failure in reporting; the raw failure is reported only when all required checks pass.
errorPrecedence.reason: Budget::work_error already keeps budget outcomes in ObjectLimit/EdgeLimit/ByteLimit/Cap/Closed/Profile, distinct from Read/Changed/File/Directory, so section 8's 'never no ancestor' is representable today
errorPrecedence.matchIsExhaustiveWithNoWildcard: a future platform variant is a compile error rather than a silent mis-map

testsToRequire: After a raw read I/O failure, every mandatory postcheck executes (assert via the existing Phase interpose seam) and each is charged against the same ledger.
Precedence in both directions: raw failure reported when all postchecks pass; postcheck error reported and the raw failure discarded when one fails.
Budget exhausted before the read: zero native callbacks, outcome unavailable or limit, never absence.
Budget exhausted during the bracket: no postcheck runs afterwards, and every later spend returns Closed.
Prepaid postchecks spend only from remaining and add nothing to used - no second charge.
A recreated cache or second ledger cannot reduce used or reopen the bracket.
Unwind through the bracket latches and leaves the reservation spent, with no refund.
Effect path: an indeterminate postcheck after a write yields unavailable, not the loser route and not a retry.
Negative compile test: the provisional outcome cannot escape the bracket.
observations: The live read_one already implements the recommended shape: it stores the read outcome, runs the after-checks with ?, and only then matches on the held outcome. The composition work is to make that bracket budgeted, not to change its order.
Section 4's publication rule is the same composition one level up, which is why no new law is needed: the raw syscall error is preserved but is not the conclusion.
Budget::capture's callback deliberately receives no budget handle, which is precisely why the prepaid bracket must open outside it.
427's ReservedPostchecks::scope is load-bearing here: a helper failure caught inside the callback still closes the owner, so an adapter cannot swallow a postcheck failure and claim a clean result.
The read buffer and the retained record are charged separately and legitimately; a future reviewer should not read that as double counting.
openQuestions: Cost derivation is the real blocker: the bracket shape is implementable with today's APIs but its numbers are not. No derivation exists for inspect_operational_file, directory_policy::inspect or check_name. The 427 account precharge is the model - a derived constant plus a test pinning observed call counts against the real algorithm.
ACL, name-service and OS-profile opaque allocations, latency, cache effects and allocator overhead remain outside these counters; the reservation bounds requested caller-owned work only.
Whether the provisional primitive belongs in platform (public and opaque) or private to security.
The edges dimension now carries native API-call counts and traversal steps on one ledger; adding postcheck syscalls sharpens that overlap and affects how operation-wide limits should be chosen.
Whether a partially completed postcheck set after a budget refusal should be distinguishable from none in diagnostics. Law makes both unavailable; only observability differs.
